access_token.description: A Segment Config API token, more details about it can be found the [Config API documentation](https://segment.com/docs/config-api/authentication/).

unsupported_destination_config_props.description:
An array of destination configuration properties which are not supported by the Segment Config API and will result in an error when applying the plan.
Properties defined here get removed from the destination configuration before calling the API. These properties will need to be defined through the UI instead.Configuration properties of type `select` are the ones resulting in an error.

config.description: The configuration of the destination. This varies according to the destination. The specific fields can be retrieved by making a request to the [Get Destination](https://reference.segmentapis.com/#94aed763-b2bd-4ee6-8b5b-b6d39aacba21) endpoint.

connection_mode.description: The connection type of the destination. Available values are: `UNSPECIFIED`, `CLOUD`, `DEVICE`.

create_time.description: The time the destination was created. *(Set by Segment)*.

display_name.description: The display name of the destination in the Segment UI. *(Set by Segment)*.

enabled.description: Whether the destination is enabled and can receive events.

parent.description: The source the destination is associated with. *(Set by Segment)*.

source.description: The Segment source name this destination is connecting to.

update_time.description: The time the destination was last updated. *(Set by Segment)*.

block.description: A destination connection on Segment. More information on destinations and how to use them can be found in the [Segment Destinations documentation](https://segment.com/docs/connections/destinations/).

condition.description: The condition of the destination filter. This is defined as a FQL statement.

description.description: The description of the destination filter for the Segment UI.

destination.description: The ID of the destination this filter is associated with.

enabled.description: Whether the destination filter is enabled.

name.description: The name of the destination fitler.

title.description: The title of the destination filter for the Segment UI.

context.description: A set of properties in the event context to either be allowed or blocked. Nested fields (i.e. dot-separated field names) are not supported.

properties.description: A set of properties in the event body to either be allowed or blocked. Nested fields (i.e. dot-separated field names) are not supported.

traits.description: A set of traits in the event body to either be allowed or blocked.

context.description: A set of properties in the event context to either be allowed or blocked. Nested fields (i.e. dot-separated field names) are not supported.

properties.description: A set of properties in the event body to either be allowed or blocked. Nested fields (i.e. dot-separated field names) are not supported.

traits.description: A set of traits in the event body to either be allowed or blocked.

block.description: Drops the event from the destination.

path.description: Events will be sampled based on the value at this path.

percent.description: The percentage of events to allow.

block.description: Allows only a percentage of events through to the destination.
The filtering action to apply to events which match the `condition` above. Available actions are: `drop`, `sample`, `block_fields`, `allow_fields`.

A destination filter which allows control of how events are flowing to destinations. More information on destination filters and how they are used can be found in the [Segment Destination Filters documentation](https://segment.com/docs/connections/destinations/destination-filters/).

catalog_name.description: The catalog name of the source.

tracking_plan.description: The ID of the associated tracking plan.

allow_group_traits_on_violations.description: Whether to allow traits of group calls on tracking plan violations.

allow_identify_traits_on_violations.description: Whether to allow traits of identify calls on tracking plan violations.

allow_track_event_on_violations.description: Whether to allow a track event on tracking plan violations.

allow_track_properties_on_violations.description: Whether to allow properties of track events on tracking plan violations.

allow_unplanned_group_traits.description: Whether to allow traits in group events not defined in the tracking plan

allow_unplanned_identify_traits.description: Whether to allow traits in identify events not defined in the tracking plan

allow_unplanned_track_event_properties.description: Whether to allow properties in track events not defined in the tracking plan.

allow_unplanned_track_events.description: Whether to allow track events not defined in the tracking plan.

common_group_event_on_violations.description: Action to take on common JSON schema violations for group events. Possible values are: `ALLOW`, `OMIT_TRAITS`, `BLOCK`.

common_identify_event_on_violations.description: Action to take on common JSON schema violations for idenify events. Possible values are: `ALLOW`, `OMIT_TRAITS`, `BLOCK`.

common_track_event_on_violations.description: Action to take on common JSON schema violations for track events. Possible values are: `ALLOW`, `OMIT_PROPERTIES`, `BLOCK`.

forwarding_blocked_events_to.description: The name of a Segment source to forward blocked events to.

forwarding_violations_to.description: The name of the Segment source to forward events with tracking plan violations.

name.description: The unique name of the source.

parent.description: The workspace the source is created in.

block.description: The configuration of the source's events.
A source connection on Segment. More information on sources and how to use them can be found in the [Segment Sources documentation](https://segment.com/docs/connections/sources/).

create_time.description: The creation time of the tracking plan. *(Set by Segment).*

display_name.description: The name of the tracking plan in the Segment UI.

import_from.description: The libraries to inherit events from, if any. Event libraries are defined as `data sources` and the `jsonencode([ ... ])` and `jsondecode()` functions should be used when including them, as per example above.

name.description: The ID of the tracking plan. *(Set by Segment).*

rules_json_file.description: The location of the JSON schema file for this tracking plan. The `file()` function should be used together with an absolute or relative path to the file.

update_time.description: The last time the tracking plan was updated. *(Set by Segment).*

block.description: A Segment tracking plan which outlines the events and properties to be collected across Segment Sources. More information can be found in the [Tracking Plans documentation](https://segment.com/docs/protocols/tracking-plan/create/).

json.description: A string representation of the json associated with an event library.

rules_json_file.description: The location of the JSON schema file containing the event library rules. The `file()` terraform function should be used and an absolute or relative path can be passed.

block.description: A data source representing an event library which is a set of common tracking plan rules which can be reused by the provider to define common attributes in multiple tracking plans.
